The goal of this analysis is to apply hierarchical clustering to the USArrests dataset to identify groups of states with similar crime profiles, and to understand how different clustering methods affect the results

In this R Markdown file, we:

    -Standardized the data

    -Computed distance matrices

    -Applied 3 hierarchical clustering methods

    -Visualized and compared clusterings

    -Projected clusters into PCA space

    -Evaluated clustering quality
```{R ???}

library(tidyverse)
library(cluster)
library(factoextra)
library(ggpubr)
library(clustertend)  # For clustering tendency


#Load data
# Using USArrests dataset; replace with your own ecological data
data <- USArrests
head(data)
summary(data)

#Standardize data
data_scaled <- scale(data)

#Check clustering tendency
get_clust_tendency(data_scaled, n = nrow(data_scaled) - 1, graph = TRUE)

#Compute distance matrix
dist_matrix <- dist(data_scaled, method = "euclidean")

#Perform hierarchical clustering (different methods)
hc_complete <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "complete")
hc_average  <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "average")
hc_single   <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "single")

#Visualize dendograms
# Basic base R dendrograms
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
plot(hc_complete, main = "Complete Linkage", xlab = "", sub = "", cex = 0.6)
plot(hc_average, main = "Average Linkage", xlab = "", sub = "", cex = 0.6)
plot(hc_single, main = "Single Linkage", xlab = "", sub = "", cex = 0.6)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

#Fancier dendograms
fviz_dend(hc_complete, k = 4, rect = TRUE, main = "Complete Linkage")
fviz_dend(hc_average,  k = 4, rect = TRUE, main = "Average Linkage")
fviz_dend(hc_single,   k = 4, rect = TRUE, main = "Single Linkage")

#Compare cluster assignments
# Cut dendrograms into 4 clusters
clust_complete <- cutree(hc_complete, k = 4)
clust_average  <- cutree(hc_average, k = 4)
clust_single   <- cutree(hc_single, k = 4)

# Combine into data frame
cluster_df <- data.frame(
  State = rownames(data),
  Complete = clust_complete,
  Average = clust_average,
  Single = clust_single
)

head(cluster_df)

# Visualize clusters in PCA
fviz_cluster(list(data = data_scaled, cluster = clust_complete),
             geom = "point", ellipse.type = "convex", palette = "jco",
             main = "Clusters (Complete Linkage) in PCA Space")
fviz_cluster(list(data = data_scaled, cluster = clust_average),
             main = "Clusters (Average Linkage)", palette = "jco")

fviz_cluster(list(data = data_scaled, cluster = clust_single),
             main = "Clusters (Single Linkage)", palette = "jco")

#Cophenetic correlation coefficients
cor_complete <- cor(dist_matrix, cophenetic(hc_complete))
cor_average  <- cor(dist_matrix, cophenetic(hc_average))
cor_single   <- cor(dist_matrix, cophenetic(hc_single))

cor_complete
cor_average
cor_single

#Add clusters to original data
data_with_clusters <- data %>%
  mutate(Cluster = factor(clust_complete))

head(data_with_clusters)
```
We calculated cophenetic correlation coefficients to evaluate how well each linkage method preserved the original data's pairwise distances. Average linkage had the highest score (0.718), closely followed by complete linkage (0.698).Single linkage performed worse (0.541), likely due to its tendency to form elongated clusters (chaining), which distort cluster relationships.
